Exercise: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
intermediate

Movement Patterns:

- unilateral_ankle_plantarflexion

Primary Muscles:

- calves

Secondary Muscles:
None

Equipment:

- dumbbell

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- ankle_strength_and_stability
- calf_muscle_hypertrophy

Contraindications:
None

Exercise Variations:

- name: Single-Leg Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise, instructions: ['Perform the exercise with one leg at a time for increased difficulty and isolation.']
- name: Dumbbell Alternating Calf Raise, instructions: ['Raise one heel while lowering the other, alternating between legs.']

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Seated Calf Raise, equipment: calf raise machine
- exercise_name: Standing Cable Calf Raise, equipment: cable machine

Instructions:

- Stand with your torso upright holding two dumbbells in your hands by your sides. Place the ball of the foot on a sturdy and stable wooden board (that is around 2-3 inches tall) while your heels extend off and touch the floor. This will be your starting position.
- With the toes pointing either straight (to hit all parts equally), inwards (for emphasis on the outer head) or outwards (for emphasis on the inner head), raise the heels off the floor as you exhale by contracting the calves. Hold the top contraction for a second.
- As you inhale, go back to the starting position by slowly lowering the heels.
- Repeat for the recommended amount of times.
